topics: An introduction to the legal system
Indian Judiciary, Doctrine of precedents, judicial review, Writ petitions, PIL–liberalization of the rule of locus standi, Judicial activism.
Introduction to environmental laws in India
General principles in Environmental law: Precautionary principle
Overview of legislations and basic concepts
Forest, Wildlife and Biodiversity related laws
Evolution and Jurisprudence of Forest and Wildlife laws
Forest policies after independence 2 Statutory framework on Forests, Wildlife and Biodiversity
Strategies for conservation–Project Tiger, Elephant, Rhino, Modulew leopard.
National Water Policy and some state policies Laws relating to prevention of pollution, access and management of water and institutional mechanism
Pollution Control Boards Ground water and law Judicial remedies and procedures Marine laws of India
Hazardous Substances and Activities Legal framework
PLI Act, 199 Principles of strict and absolute liability
signature, ratification Evolution of international environmental law

partA.description: 2 Questions from each module.  Total of 8 Questions, each carrying 3 marks

partB.description: Each question carries 9 marks.  Two questions will be given from each module, out of which 1 question should be answered.  Each question can have a maximum of 3 sub divisions.

courseOutcomes.description: Familiar with the laws, policies and institutions in the field of environment
Acquire the skills needed for interpreting laws, policies and judicial decisions in a holistic perspective
Acquire the ability to evaluate the role of law and policy in conservation and management of natural resources and prevention of pollution
Familiar with the concept of international environmental law
